full_judgment:
10. Mr. Md. Hefzul Bari, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the High Court Division passed the impugned judgment and order on erroneous and wrong findings that the writ petitioner is entitled to pension and other benefits taking his date of birth to be 01.01.1952 since his actual date of birth as per office record is 02.04.1950. The appointment of the writ petitioner-respondent herein took place on 1967 at which time the writ petitioner must have been at least 18 years of age, as under-aged appointment of employee is in contravention to BADC's Service Rules. Therefore, the impugned judgment and order has been passed on incorrect application of the law and is liable to be set aside. He further submitted that the High Court Division erred in law and on facts by not considering the fact that even if it is concluded that the date of birth of the writ petitioner should be counted from 01.01.1952 as per his Secondary School Certificate, it would mean that the writ petitioner was only 16 years old, a minor, at the time of appointment in 1967. Consequently, this amounts to a clear mis-representation of the writ petitioner's age and in violation of the BADC's relevant Service Rules. He lastly submitted that the impugned judgment and order was passed on erroneous grounds and without considering that when the petitioner filed a representation addressed to writ respondent No. 2 requesting the respondent to consider his date of birth as 01.01.1952, in the same letter, the writ petitioner acknowledged that he had joined the service of BADC at the age of 16. As such, if the impugned judgment and order is allowed to continue, the writ petitioner would be illegally benefited by claiming salaries for the first two years of his service from 1967 while at the same time claiming the present pension and other retirement benefits taking his date of birth from 01.01.1952. Therefore, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. 

 13. The main point in controversy is the date of birth of respondent Md. Abdus Salam. The BADC relied on the date of birth as 02.04.1950 as per the office record. However, the respondent Md. Abdus Salam claims that his date of birth is 01.01.1952 according to his S.S.C. Certificate. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submitted that if the date of birth as claimed by the respondent-writ petitioner as 01.01.1952 is taken to be correct then he would have been less than 18 years old at the time of his appointment, and his appointment would have been illegal. 

 14. We find from the record that there was a fire in the record room of BADC which resulted in many records being destroyed, including the records relating to the writ petitioner-respondent herein. We also find that in compliance with the direction of BADC, the writ petitioner furnished his S.S.C. Certificate along with a photocopy in 1997. Consequently, BADC issued a notice indicating that the writ petitioner would retire on 01.01.2009. But subsequently BADC issued the office order dated 26.11.2008 to the effect that the petitioner's retirement was effective from 02.4.2007, i.e. taking his date of birth to be 02.04.1950.
